docs.text: VerityRisk User Documentation VerityRisk is a Segregation of Duties (SoD) application. It loads operator access from one or more Syspro sources, evaluates that access against a ruleset, and highlights conflicts. You can then mitigate those conflicts by location or by operator, with an optional approval process. Note Menu items are shown only when your role includes the matching permission. If a page described here is missing from your menu, ask an administrator to review your role. Using the application Most list pages share the same table tools: Search filters every visible column. Column filters narrow the list by a specific field. Click a column heading to sort. Clear Filter resets the current filters. Export downloads the current view as an XLSX file. Page size options are typically 10, 25, or 50 rows. Edit screens often open as a dialog over the list. Use the page back control or close the dialog to return to the list. docs.text: Configuration The Configuration page controls when VerityRisk loads source data and how long snapshots are kept. Permission: AdminConfigurationUpdate Open Configuration Navigate to Administration >> Configuration . Field Editable Description Load Schedule Yes Cron expression for the permission and violation load. The default is 0 5-20 * * * (hourly from 05:00 to 20:00). Load Schedule Description No Human-readable form of the load schedule Snapshot Schedule Yes Cron expression for database snapshots. The default is 0 4 * * * (daily at 04:00). Snapshot Schedule Description No Human-readable form of the snapshot schedule Snapshot Retention Days Yes How long snapshots are kept. The default is 180 . Update the schedule Edit Load Schedule , Snapshot Schedule , and Snapshot Retention Days as needed. Use standard five-field cron syntax. Click Save . Confirm that the description fields update to match the new expressions. A Configuration Updated message confirms the save. Warning An invalid load schedule is rejected. Correct the cron expression and save again. The load processes every active source , then recalculates violations against the current ruleset. Related pages Sources

The scheduled load (see Configuration ) pulls permission data from every active source, then evaluates it against the ruleset. Permission: AdminSourceUpdate Open the source list Navigate to Administration >> Sources . Column Description Business Key Short code for the instance (also used as the business unit) Business Unit Name Display name Source Type Syspro7 or Syspro8 Is Active Whether the source is included in loads Add or edit a source Click Add , or click Edit on an existing source. docs.text: The Rule Violation Mitigation Approval Process VerityRisk has an optional opt-in mitigation approval process. This feature allows you to assign specific rules to an approval role, for better controls around rule violation mitigations. Note Approval is only applicable for the Mitigation By Operator method at this point in time. For the day-to-day screens, see Cancel Mitigations and Approve/Reject Mitigations . Creating an Approval Role Any role that is assigned the RuleMitigationApprove permission is able to approve a mitigation for any rules that have this role as the Approver Role . E.g. In this example I have created a custom role called Mitigation Approver that is assigned the RuleMitigationApprove permission. This role is able to approve mitigation requests for rules that have this role assigned as the Approver Role . Assigning Approver Roles to Rules Now if we edit an existing rule we can fill in the Approver Role field if violations of this rule require mitigation approval. If rule violations do not require approval we can set the Approver Role field back to No approver . Note Only roles with the RuleMitigationApprove permission are selectable in the Approver Role dropdown. Creating a mitigation that requires approval When you are performing a Mitigation By Operator , if the potential mitigation has an Approver Role assigned, then once the user selects Update Operator Mitigations the rule violation mitigations will be assigned to any user with the assigned Approver Role to approve or reject the mitigation. In this case any user with the custom Mitigation Approver role will be able to approve or reject the mitigation. If you created a mitigation by mistake, open Cancel Mitigations . It shows the pending requests that you captured. Note You can only cancel mitigations that you created. To cancel a mitigation waiting for approval, just select the mitigation(s) you want to cancel, add a comment if needed and click the Cancel button. Approving a mitigation If you log in as a user that has a role with the RuleMitigationApprove permission, then you can select the Approve/Reject Mitigations tab to approve or reject rule violation mitigations. In the same way as canceling mitigations, you just select the mitigations that you wish to approve (or reject), add an optional comment and click on the Approve or Reject button. Note Mitigations are marked Currently Mitigated on Mitigation By Operator and in the PowerBI SoD reports only after they are approved.
docs.title: The Rule Violation Mitigation Approval Process

docs.text: Approve/Reject Mitigations Approve/Reject Mitigations is where users with an approver role accept or reject pending operator mitigation requests. Permission: RuleMitigationApprove Note You cannot approve a request that you captured yourself. The original capturer can withdraw it on Cancel Mitigations . Note You only see requests for rules whose Approver Role is a role assigned to you. Location mitigations never appear here. Open Approve/Reject Mitigations Navigate to approvals >> Approve/Reject Mitigations . The menu label includes a count of requests waiting for you, for example Approve/Reject Mitigations (5) . Column Description Rule ID Rule the mitigation applies to Business Unit Source instance Operator Operator affected by the request Ticket Number Ticket attached when the request was submitted Approver Role Name Role required to approve the request Action MitigationAdd or MitigationRemove Only Pending requests are shown. Approve or reject Select one or more pending mitigations. You must belong to the Approver Role on each selected rule. Optionally enter a Comment (up to 150 characters). Click Approve or Reject . Confirm the comment, the action, and the number of selected items. Click Confirm Changes , or Back to return without deciding. If nothing is selected, VerityRisk shows No mitigation approvals selected . What happens next Decision Result Approve The add or remove is applied. The violation is marked Currently Mitigated (or no longer mitigated) on Mitigation By Operator and in the PowerBI SoD reports. Reject The request is closed and access is not changed. The violation reappears on Mitigation By Operator. Related pages Mitigation By Operator Cancel Mitigations Roles The Rule Violation Mitigation Approval Process

docs.text: Cancel Mitigations Cancel Mitigations lets you withdraw operator mitigation requests that you submitted and that are still waiting for approval. Click Confirm Changes , or Back to return without cancelling. If nothing is selected, VerityRisk shows No mitigation approvals selected . Note Cancelled requests do not change Currently Mitigated on Mitigation By Operator . The underlying violation reappears on that list so you can submit it again if needed. docs.text: Rule List The Rule List is where you browse SoD processes and maintain the rules that detect conflicting access. Permission: RuleView to open the list. RuleUpdate to add or edit a rule. Open the process list Navigate to Home >> Rule List . The Process List shows every process in the ruleset. Column Description Key Process business key Description Process name Rule Count Number of rules in the process Click View on a process to open its rule list. Review rules in a process The rule list title is {process key} Rule List . Use the back control to return to the process list. Column Description ID Rule ID within the process Risk Rating High, Medium, or Critical Access Rule Access Risk Description of the access risk Transaction A Transaction on side A of the conflict Transaction B Transaction on side B of the conflict Approver Role Role that must approve operator mitigations for this rule, or No approver You can search, filter, sort, and export this list. Add a rule Open the rule list for the process. Click Add . Complete the New/Update Rule form (see Rule fields ). Click Save . A Rule updated message confirms the change. Note New rules default to risk rating Medium . The process field is set for you and cannot be changed. Rule ID plus process must be unique. Edit a rule Click Edit on the rule. Update the fields. Click Save . Rule fields Field Notes Process Read-only. Shown as description and business key. Rule ID Up to 10 characters. Suffix after the process key. Risk Rating High , Medium , or Critical Access . Probability 1 through 5 . Source Type Syspro or FlowCentric (not implemented yet). SAP Rule ID Optional external identifier (up to 100 characters). Access Risk Description of the risk. Transaction A Side A transaction (up to 100 characters). Transaction B Side B transaction (up to 100 characters). Program A Syspro programs on side A. All selected programs must be granted. Program B Syspro programs on side B. Activities A Syspro activities on side A. All selected activities must be granted. Activities B Syspro activities on side B. Approver Role Role that approves operator mitigations for this rule. Only roles with the RuleMitigationApprove permission appear. Choose No approver if mitigations should apply immediately. A rule defines a conflict between side A and side B . A side can use programs, activities, or both. You can also define a one-sided rule by filling in only side A or only side B. Note When Approver Role is set, operator mitigations for that rule wait for approval. See The Rule Violation Mitigation Approval Process . Note FlowCentric appears as a source type on the form, but it is not implemented yet. Related pages Violation Explorer - test which rules a proposed access combination would violate Mitigation By Operator Mitigation By Location

docs.text: Violation Explorer Violation Explorer lets you test which segregation-of-duty rules would be violated for a proposed combination of groups, roles, and activities. Use it to explore access before it is granted, or to understand why an operator already appears as a violation. Permission: RuleExplorerView Note This screen does not change mitigations or operator access. It only calculates what the current ruleset would report. Open Violation Explorer Navigate to Home >> Violation Explorer . Calculate violations Select a Business Unit . This loads the groups, roles, activities, and operators for that Syspro source. Optionally select Load from Operator . The operator's current groups, roles, and activities are copied into the form so you can start from a real profile. Adjust Groups , Roles , and Activities as needed. Groups is required. Click Calculate Violations . If nothing matches the ruleset, a No violations found message is shown. Results Column Description Rule ID Rule that would be violated Program A / Program B Programs on each side of the rule Activities A / Activities B Activities on each side of the rule Business Unit Source instance used for the calculation Company Code / Company Name Company in which the conflict occurs Access Type How the two sides of the rule are reached: Group , Role , or Hybrid Access Code A / Access Code B Group or role that satisfies each side Risk Rating Risk rating from the rule You can search, filter, sort, and export the results. Access types Group - both sides of the rule are reached through group program grants. Role - both sides are reached through role grants in the same company. Hybrid - one side is reached through a group and the other through a role. Related pages Rule List
docs.title: Violation Explorer

docs.text: Mitigation By Location Mitigation By Location applies a control to every operator at selected locations for a given rule. Permission: RuleMitigateView to open the list. RuleMitigateUpdate to save location changes. Warning Location mitigations take effect immediately. There is no approval step. Tip Use Mitigation By Operator when you need to mitigate individual operators instead of whole locations. Open the location list Navigate to Mitigation >> Mitigation By Location . Enter a Document Number (required, up to 50 characters). Enter a Document Description (required, up to 2000 characters). In the Locations table, select the locations that should be mitigated. docs.text: Mitigation By Operator Mitigation By Operator applies a control to specific rule violations for individual operators. Each change is recorded against a mitigation ticket . Permission: RuleMitigateView to open the page. RuleMitigateUpdate to submit changes. Note If the rule has an Approver Role , the change waits for approval instead of applying immediately. See The Rule Violation Mitigation Approval Process . Tip Use Mitigation By Location when the same control should cover every operator at a location. Open Mitigation By Operator Navigate to Mitigation >> Mitigation By Operator . The Mitigate By Operator page shows current violations. Rows that are already mitigated are pre-selected. Column Description Rule ID Rule that was violated Rule Risk Rating Risk rating from the rule Rule Access Risk Description of the access risk Operator Full Name Operator with the conflict Business Unit Source instance Access Access pair that caused the violation Ticket Number Ticket currently attached, if the violation is already mitigated Approver Role Role that must approve changes, if the rule requires approval Currently Mitigated Whether this violation is already mitigated You can search, filter, sort, select all, and export this list. Note Violations that are waiting for approval are hidden from this list until they are approved, rejected, or cancelled. Add or remove operator mitigations Create an Active ticket on Mitigation Tickets if you do not already have one. Select a Ticket Number . This field is required. Select the violations that should be mitigated. Clear the selection for violations that should no longer be mitigated. Click Update Operator Mitigations . Confirm the change: Operators Added is the number of newly selected, previously unmitigated violations. Operators Removed is the number of previously mitigated violations you cleared. Click Confirm Changes to submit, or Back to return without saving. A Mitigation by operators updated message confirms the save. If you did not change any selections, VerityRisk shows No mitigation operators changed . What happens after you confirm Rule configuration Result Approver Role is No approver The add or remove is applied immediately. Currently Mitigated updates on this page and in the PowerBI SoD reports. Approver Role is set A pending approval is created. The violation stays off this list until an approver acts, or until you cancel it. You can cancel your own pending requests on Cancel Mitigations . Approvers act on Approve/Reject Mitigations . The Action on a pending request is MitigationAdd or MitigationRemove , depending on whether you selected or cleared the violation. Related pages Mitigation Tickets Cancel Mitigations Approve/Reject Mitigations The Rule Violation Mitigation Approval Process

docs.text: Mitigation Tickets A mitigation ticket is the control document you attach when you mitigate a rule violation by operator. Create the ticket first, then select it on Mitigation By Operator . Permission: RuleMitigationTicketView to open the list. RuleMitigationTicketUpdate to add or edit a ticket. Note Location mitigations do not use tickets. They use a document number and description instead. See Mitigation By Location . Open the ticket list Navigate to Mitigation >> Mitigation Tickets . Column Description Ticket Number Identifier shown when mitigating by operator Created By User who created the ticket Active Whether the ticket can be selected for new mitigations You can search, filter, sort, and export this list. Add a ticket Click Add . Enter a Ticket Number (up to 100 characters). Enter an Audit Control Description (up to 500 characters). Leave Active on unless you are creating a ticket that should not be used yet. New tickets default to active. Click Save . A Mitigation ticket updated message confirms the change. Edit a ticket Click Edit on the ticket. Update the ticket number, description, or active flag. Click Save . Note Only Active tickets appear in the Ticket Number dropdown on Mitigation By Operator. Deactivating a ticket records who deactivated it and when. Existing operator mitigations that already use the ticket are not removed. Related pages Mitigation By Operator The Rule Violation Mitigation Approval Process
